pattern.description: The 2x2 tile grid re-lays out: the suitcase tile grows into a tall hero tile, the kayak tile enlarges, the bottom two shrink to thumbnails, the SDK icon column shifts left, and a Booking confirmed chip pops onto the hero tile.
pattern.why_premium: Re-weighting the grid instead of cutting puts one use case in focus while keeping the others visible, and the chip lands a concrete outcome on the image as the narration says 'creating apps'.

build_hint.gsap: Use Flip: const state = Flip.getState('.tile, .sdk-icon'); apply the hero layout class; Flip.from(state, {duration: 0.7, ease: 'power3.inOut', absolute: true}); then tl.fromTo('.chip', {scale: 0.6, opacity: 0}, {scale: 1, opacity: 1, duration: 0.3, ease: 'back.out(1.6)'}, '-=0.35');
build_hint.remotion: Interpolate each tile's x, y, width, height between the two layouts with p = spring({frame, fps, config: {damping: 200}}); chip scale = spring({frame: frame - 10, fps, config: {damping: 10, stiffness: 180}}) mapped 0.6->1 with opacity interpolate over 4 frames.

notes: Camera verdict none; raw scale 1.13 is the tiles resizing inside the frame. Chip could also be read as chip_append; layout_reframe chosen as the dominant motion. Tile boxes are manual because only a union diff box covers the grid.
